finding: Studies how solid materials such as fabrics and plastics burn under different airflow speeds and oxygen levels in microgravity.
Large fire tests run inside uncrewed cargo vehicles to see how a fire grows in a spacecraft-sized volume.
Measures smoke particles from overheated spacecraft materials to help design smoke detectors that work in microgravity.
Tests detection of dust and aerosols in microgravity, which matters where dust can trigger false alarms.
Burns fuel droplets and studies how flames go out when the chamber air is diluted with CO2 or helium.
Studies cool flames: low-temperature burning that can continue without a visible flame.
Six gaseous-fuel flame experiments run in the Combustion Integrated Rack to understand basic flame behaviour.
Future lunar bases and pressurized rovers may use about 30% or more oxygen at 10.2 psi or less, which makes materials more flammable.
Spacesuits run at 4.3 psi with 100% oxygen, so anything inside a suit faces a very oxygen-rich environment.
Upcoming experiments that will add partial-gravity (Moon) flammability data.
